title: Rigveda 4.56: To Heaven and earth
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.56: To Heaven and earth: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.56 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Heaven and earth. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 314v-315v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.56.1 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 314v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ma̱hī dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī i̱ha jyeṣṭhe̍ ru̱cā bha̍vatāṁ śu̱caya̍dbhir a̱rkaiḥ | yat sī̱ṁ vari̍ṣṭhe bṛha̱tī vi̍mi̱nvan ru̱vad dho̱kṣā pa̍prathā̱nebhi̱r evai̍ḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>MAY mighty Heaven and Earth, most meet for honour, be present here with light and gleaming splendours; When, fixing them apart, vast, most extensive, the Steer roars loudly in far-reaching courses.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 314v (numbered 123v by the scribe) (OPenn image 315, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.55.6 ‹-api ebhiḥ iṣṭaiḥ samudram›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 315r (numbered 124r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.56.2 ‹-aminatī iti tasthatuḥ ukṣamāṇeiti›. Verse 4.56.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>mahī | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | iha | jyeṣṭheiti | rucā | bhavatām | śucayat-bhiḥ | arkaiḥ | yat | sīm | variṣṭheiti | bṛhatī iti | vi-minvan | ruvat | ha | ukṣā | paprathānebhiḥ | evaiḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 4.56.2-6 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 315r
translation.original_text:
2de̱vī de̱vebhi̍r yaja̱te yaja̍trai̱r ami̍natī tasthatur u̱kṣamā̍ṇe | ṛ̱tāva̍rī a̱druhā̍ de̱vapu̍tre ya̱jñasya̍ ne̱trī śu̱caya̍dbhir a̱rkaiḥ ||
3sa it svapā̱ bhuva̍neṣv āsa̱ ya i̱me dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī ja̱jāna̍ | u̱rvī ga̍bhī̱re raja̍sī su̱meke̍ ava̱ṁśe dhīra̱ḥ śacyā̱ sam ai̍rat ||
4nū ro̍dasī bṛ̱hadbhi̍r no̱ varū̍thai̱ḥ patnī̍vadbhir i̱ṣaya̍ntī sa̱joṣā̍ḥ | u̱rū̱cī viśve̍ yaja̱te ni pā̍taṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
5pra vā̱m mahi̱ dyavī̍ a̱bhy upa̍stutim bharāmahe | śucī̱ upa̱ praśa̍staye ||
6pu̱nā̱ne ta̱nvā̍ mi̱thaḥ svena̱ dakṣe̍ṇa rājathaḥ | ū̱hyāthe̍ sa̱nād ṛ̱tam ||
translation.text:
2The Goddesses with Gods, holy with holy, the Two stand pouring out their rain, exhaustless: Faithful and guileless, having Gods for children, leaders of sacrifice with shining splendours.
3Sure in the worlds he was a skilful Craftsman, he who produced these Twain the Earth and Heaven. Wise, with his power he brought both realms, together spacious and deep, wellfashioned, unsupported.
4O Heaven and Earth, with one accord promoting, with high protection as of Queens, our welfare, Far-reaching, universal, holy, guard us. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
5To both of you, O Heaven and Earth, we bring our lofty song of praise, Pure Ones! to glorify you both.
6Ye sanctify each other's form, by your own proper might ye rule, And from of old observe the Law.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 315r (numbered 124r by the scribe) (OPenn image 315, lower leaf). 3saḥ | it | su-apāḥ | bhuvaneṣu | āsa | yaḥ | ime iti | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | jajāna | urvī iti | gabhīre iti | rajasī iti | sumeke itisu-meke | avaṃśe | dhīraḥ | śacyā | sam | airat
4nu | rodasī iti | bṛhat-bhiḥ | naḥ | varūthaiḥ | patnīvat-bhiḥ | iṣayantī iti | sa-joṣāḥ | urūcī iti | viśveiti | yājate iti | ni | pātam | dhiyā | syāma | rathyaḥ | sadāsāḥ
5pra | vām | mahi | dyavī iti | abhi | upa-stutim | bharāmahe | śucī iti | upa | pra-śastaye
6punāne iti | tanvā | mithaḥ | svena | dakṣeṇa | rājathaḥ | ūhyātheiti | sanāt | ṛtam

translation.original_ref: RV 4.56.7 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 315v
translation.original_text: <sup>7</sup>ma̱hī mi̱trasya̍ sādhatha̱s tara̍ntī̱ pipra̍tī ṛ̱tam | pari̍ ya̱jñaṁ ni ṣe̍dathuḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>7</sup>Furthering and fulfilling, ye, O Mighty, perfect Mitra's Law. Ye sit around our sacrifice.
